source.training_license_gate: Use only rows whose per-row provenance explicitly verifies CC0-1.0.

hypothesis: A generalized ranked-probability loss on ordered Score decisions improves held-out ordinal probability quality without sacrificing the broader typed-decision gate.

evaluation.baseline: Pinned released Open-Jev checkpoint on the same selected rows.
evaluation.candidate: Same frozen train/calibration/test/OOD selections and training settings as the source protocol, changing only the optional ordinal RPS weight from 0 to 0.5.
evaluation.primary_metric: Mean ranked probability score on Score decisions in the preregistered OOD split.
secondary_metrics: Overall and per-kind negative log likelihood

retention_gate: Retain only as a research candidate if OOD Score RPS is lower than the released checkpoint, overall OOD top-1 is no lower, overall OOD NLL is lower, and no decision kind loses more than 5 percentage points of top-1 accuracy. Otherwise reject the ablation.
limitations: This compares with public Open-Jev, not proprietary TypeSafe Jev.
The OOD split was used in the source protocol and this is a retrospective ablation, not an independent confirmation.
No TypeSafe Jev outputs are collected, used as labels, used for tuning, or reused.
This does not demonstrate desktop task success, authorization, or execution safety.
